response.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, order_count * 1.0 / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM matched

assumptions.assumption: Distinct orders are identified by orders.recordvault, the unique order reference that risk/margin records link to. Using orders.orderspivot would give the same result if recordvault is unique per order.

The 'average of those numbers across scopes' is the average of the per-scope distinct order counts. It is taken over the scopes that remain after the inner joins, so scopes with no matched orders are not included.
A NULL acctscope, if any matched user has one, is kept as its own group.
